title: Device chronicle & temporal pin workflow for hardware-specific perf profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: When publishing hardware-specific performance profiles we lack a standardized temporal metadata and delta-aggregation strategy. This causes noisy re-publishing, unclear pin rollback windows, and inconsistent client pin behavior across GPUs (A100/H100/L40S/MI300).

Goal: Implement a device chronicle and 'temporal pin' workflow that: (1) publishes per-device delta signatures instead of only absolute snapshots, (2) records a temporal window + canary cohort metadata for each publish, and (3) exposes a clear rollback/auto-revert policy surfaced in the model catalog and SDKs. The outcome should reduce noisy churn on pins, make canary rollouts deterministic across hardware variants, and enable safer automated re-pinning after transient performance regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Device chronicle schema defined and documented in Confluence (link below)
Publish API extended to accept and serve 'delta_signature' and 'temporal_window' fields
Model catalog UI shows temporal pin metadata and canary cohort for each hardware profile
SDK pin resolver honors temporal window and canary cohort when choosing a pinned model variant
Integration tests validate rollback-on-degrade and auto-revert behavior for simulated HW regressions
Perf dashboards show reduction in manual pin reverts (target: 30% fewer re-pins over 30 days)
implementation_steps: Design device chronicle JSON schema (fields: device_sku, baseline_signature, delta_signature, sample_count, timestamp, temporal_window, cohort_tag)
Add DB table 'device_chronicles' and migration; wire into profile publisher service (runtime-profile-publisher)
API change: POST /profiles/publish accepts optional 'delta_signature' and 'temporal_window' (start,end) strings
Server: compute rolling-signature by stitching per-device deltas across sample buckets (fast path for identical deltas)
SDK: implement pin resolver update to prefer active temporal pins and evaluate cohort membership (user-region, tier) before fallback
Console: render temporal window badge and cohort list; add timeline view to inspect historic chronicles
QA: create synthetic workload harness to simulate cold/warm tails for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 and run canary experiments
Rollout: feature flag behind 'device-chronicle' with staged rollout to internal customers then public
decisions: Use delta_signature (sha256 of summarized latency/cost vectors) instead of full histogram blobs to reduce storage and diffing cost
Temporal window will be inclusive and defined in UTC ISO timestamps; SDKs interpret as best-effort and fall back to static pin when clock skew prevents evaluation
Cohort selection implemented server-side; SDK receives cohort_tag and evaluation inputs (region, customer_tier) to avoid exposing internal routing logic
Auto-revert policy: 72-hour hold window for new temporal pins unless a stability threshold is reached earlier (configurable per-project)
Stitching algorithm: weighted median of per-device delta-signatures with outlier dampening (to avoid single-device noise flipping pins)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SDK mis-evaluates temporal windows leading to inconsistent pin choice across clients — Mitigation: publish 'pin_evaluation_decision' debug logs and add opt-in verbose mode for customers
Risk: Delta-signature collisions or noisy fingerprints — Mitigation: include sample_count and model_version in signature input and fall back to full-histogram compare if suspicious
Risk: Increased storage/compute for chronicle ingestion — Mitigation: TTL retention policy for per-device diaries and compression for historic archives
Risk: Canary cohort mis-targeting can cause customer impact — Mitigation: simulate cohorts in staging and gate promotion with manual review for first 3 publishes
